stem: A provider prescribes promethazine for an 18-month-old child. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer the medication because promethazine is safer in children under 2 years.
options.B: Hold the medication and clarify the order because promethazine must not be used in children younger than 2 years.
options.C: Give a double dose because young children clear the medication rapidly.
options.D: Administer it only if the child has no fever.

rationale: Promethazine is contraindicated in pediatric patients younger than 2 years because postmarketing cases of respiratory depression, including fatalities, have occurred in this age group. The nurse should not administer the medication and should clarify the prescription.
educational_objective: Recognize the pediatric age contraindication for promethazine.
source_locator: Boxed Warning / Contraindications—Pediatric patients younger than 2 years; risk of fatal respiratory depression
source_claim_supported: Promethazine must not be used in children younger than 2 years because of potentially fatal respiratory depression.
correction_summary: Converted the item to an age-specific medication-safety action and removed repetitive cueing.
audit_findings: Age 18 months directly triggers the labeled contraindication.
Other options do not address the boxed warning.
Independent second pass confirmed a unique key.
